title: NormGym finds current language-model agents struggle to infer new social norms
summary: NormGym evaluates agents that must infer hidden norms through interaction while pursuing a task. The strongest evaluated LLM achieved 55.3% joint task-and-compliance success. Models sometimes changed behavior after sanctions directed at themselves but struggled to infer norms from other agents’ behavior and sanctions; fine-tuning was not sufficient in the reported tests.
ai_technology: NormGym interactive benchmark with large-language-model agents
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed arXiv metadata

evidence.tested: LLM agents were evaluated on hidden-norm tasks across benchmark environments; the strongest model’s joint task-and-compliance success was 55.3%, and peer-behavior cues remained difficult to use.
evidence.unknown: The findings concern the evaluated agents and benchmark norms/environments; transfer to real communities is not established.
evidence.ai_role: LLM agents interact with simulated communities, observe behavior and sanctions, and attempt to infer and apply hidden norms.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
